profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the WhatsCode research evaluation workstream and the ML platform telemetry workstream ahead of an internal governance review and a draft paper appendix on large-scale GenAI deployment for developer efficiency at WhatsApp. The immediate context is that the team needs a single telemetry handoff covering the latest quarterly rollout, including counts of accepted changes, collaboration-pattern labels, and coverage numbers, so the research side can update longitudinal analyses while the platform side prepares matching figures for leadership. The agenda is to align on which snapshot will be handed off, what the coverage table should contain, what counts as an accepted change in the summary, and how the shared artifact will be delivered. The expected outcome is an apparently clear agreement that Leo will provide the 'Q2 rollout bundle' by Friday and Nisha will use it to refresh the research notebook and governance slides.

members.name: Dr. Nisha Raman
members.expertise: Longitudinal evaluation of developer-assistance systems, annotation design, productivity measurement, and compliance-related ML studies
members.background: Nisha leads the research analysis stream for WhatsCode and previously worked on empirical software engineering studies of code assistants in regulated environments.
members.private_state: She wants a stable, publication-quality dataset that she can cite consistently across the internal review and the draft manuscript, and she is trying to avoid last-minute remapping of telemetry fields or denominator changes that would force her to rerun prior analyses.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'Q2 snapshot,' they mean the quarter-end research extract containing all merged changes up to the final calendar day, even if some have not fully propagated through release trains.
An 'accepted change' is any AI-generated or AI-assisted code change that was merged after human review, counted at the pull-request level regardless of later operational outcomes like revert windows.
The 'coverage' table for this project naturally refers to privacy verification coverage, because that is the historically tracked longitudinal series in the study.
A handoff that is 'ready' means an immutable parquet or table snapshot in the research bucket with a frozen schema so analyses remain reproducible.
If Leo says the numbers will match leadership reporting, that will still be compatible with the research team's existing definitions after light field renaming.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.role: Applied ML Platform Engineer, Developer Intelligence Infrastructure
members.expertise: Telemetry pipelines, CI/CD integrations, production rollout monitoring, and operational reporting for code-generation systems
members.background: Leo owns the instrumentation and dashboard exports used to monitor WhatsCode deployments across codegen, policy automation, bug triage, and framework migration workflows.
members.private_state: He wants to satisfy the research request using existing operational exports rather than creating a custom research dataset, and he is focused on keeping the numbers consistent with the dashboard used by leadership and compliance ops.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the 'Q2 snapshot,' they mean the latest release-train cut used in production reporting, because anything else will not reconcile with leadership dashboards.
An 'accepted change' should exclude changes reverted within the standard stabilization window and is best counted using landed diff batches rather than raw reviewed pull requests.
The 'coverage' number should include all automated policy-checking surfaces currently exposed through WhatsCode, not just privacy verification, because the platform reports them together.
A dataset that is 'ready by Friday' can be the existing dashboard CSV export in the shared analytics folder, even if it refreshes automatically over the weekend.
If Nisha needs collaboration-pattern analysis, she can derive it from the existing export fields without a separately frozen research artifact.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to report the number of 'accepted changes' in the Q2 bundle.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means AI-generated or AI-assisted changes that were merged after human review, counted at the pull-request level even if some were later reverted or squashed into downstream fixes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means changes that survived the post-submit stabilization window and are counted from landed production diff batches, excluding reverted items and sometimes collapsing multiple reviewed PRs into one operational unit.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term is already institutionalized in both research slides and ops dashboards, so each assumes the other is using the organization's standard meaning; because both meanings produce plausible totals, nothing sounds obviously inconsistent during a quick coordination call.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'Q2 snapshot' is being handed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using the 'Q2 snapshot' or the 'latest quarterly snapshot' for the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the quarter-end research extract keyed to all merges through June 30 across active branches used for longitudinal analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the production reporting snapshot generated from the Monday release-train cut that leadership uses for quarterly operational summaries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are commonly called the quarterly snapshot internally and are usually close in date, so the shared label creates false consensus without triggering clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the bundle should include the updated 'coverage table' for the review deck.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects the table to cover only privacy verification coverage, preserving the same denominator as the 15% to 53% historical series in the study.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the table to include all policy-automation surfaces currently tracked in the platform dashboard, such as privacy, reliability, and security template checks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because privacy is the flagship example in the project narrative and the broader dashboard also uses the word 'coverage,' each assumes the other implicitly knows which subset is the natural one for this audience.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a 'ready' Friday handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Leo will have the telemetry 'ready by Friday' for Nisha to plug into the notebook.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a frozen, versioned parquet or table snapshot in the research bucket with a stable schema and no further automatic updates.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to drop a CSV export from the existing dashboard into the shared folder, where it will continue refreshing on the normal schedule.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The meeting is about coordination rather than technical packaging, and both see the delivery method as routine plumbing; 'ready' sounds sufficiently concrete that neither thinks to unpack file format, immutability, or refresh behavior.
